data.name: Katibah
data.gender_notes: Katibah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A female scribe or writer. Derived from the Arabic word 'katibah' meaning 'she who writes'. In Islamic tradition, writing is a noble and respected profession, and those who excel in this skill are highly valued. The name Katibah carries the meaning “Scribe, Writer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Katibah usually hope their child will grow to embody scribe, writer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Katibah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Scribe, Writer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Katibah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

It emphasizes the legacy of scholars and intellectuals who have contributed significantly to Islamic history through their writings. A girl named Katibah would be a constant reminder of this rich literary heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Katibah" has spiritual significance as it associates the bearer with the divine art of writing. In Islamic tradition, it is believed that everything recorded in the Quran was written by the divine hand of Allah. So, a Katibah holds a special connection with Allah, as she is imbued with the skill of putting words onto paper, shaping and transmitting knowledge. It also represents the importance of documenting deeds and memories, reminding us of the value of preserving our experiences for future generations to learn from.
